  WHY: The referenced procedure covers sessions older than 72 hours or cases where the pickup is down, so the pointer can leave operators without an applicable recovery path or lead them to bypass the safeguard.

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- .claude/scripts/usage_limit_resumes.py: is_limit_wait, the has_limit_text early return at lines 352-353 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  PROBLEM: has_limit_text returns True on any limit-text substring without constraining trailing actionable text, so is_limit_wait returns True for mixed limit text and an action verb outside HUMAN_REQUEST_PATTERN.
  WHY: A session with a pending human instruction can be resumed before the human responds, defeating the ask-first guard.
- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/usage_limit_resumes.py: is_limit_wait, the has_limit_text early return at lines 352-353 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  PROBLEM: Same issue as the twin. The synced root copy is byte-identical and has the same bypass: has_limit_text returns True on any limit-text substring without constraining trailing actionable text. Both copies must be fixed together.
  WHY: Identical runtime failure path as the twin — a session with a pending human instruction whose verb is outside HUMAN_REQUEST_PATTERN is resumed.
- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/usage_limit_resumes.py: _skip_reason, lines 468-470 (too_old) returning before lines 478-481 (needs_input) | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  PROBLEM: The too_old check returns before has_unanswered_request, so an old session with an unanswered human request is classified as too_old rather than needs_input.
  WHY: An operator following the handbook guidance manually resumes an old session that still has an unanswered question or approval request, and the resumed session acts on the pending decision.
- tests/test_usage_limit_resumes.py: test_a_limit_wait_that_also_asks_a_human_is_skipped (lines 267-281) and test_is_limit_wait (lines 300-323) | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  PROBLEM: Neither test table covers limit-error text combined with an actionable instruction whose verb is outside HUMAN_REQUEST_PATTERN.
  WHY: The tests pass without detecting the mixed-text bypass in is_limit_wait, so a session with a pending action can be resumed in production.
- changelog.d/6102-skip-unanswered-question-resumes.md: Line 12, "Wording the selector does not recognise counts as a request, so such a session stays with the manual resume in docs/operations/master-session.md." | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: The changelog points operators to manual-resume guidance that does not describe a procedure for resuming a recent session whose needs_action wording the selector failed to recognize as a request.
  WHY: An operator may manually resume a session with a pending human decision, defeating the safety fix; alternatively, the session stays stopped indefinitely with no documented recovery path.

  WHY: has_unanswered_request returns False for sessions whose summaries contain actionable human requests alongside limit text, so the selector queues an automated resume trigger for an idle session waiting on human action or authorization.
